passage:
In the block corner of the nursery, Suraj set the last block on top and his tower wobbled, then stood.
"Look at me! I did it all by myself!"
Wasim, the teacher, came over and crouched down. "I see. You put the big blocks at the bottom and the small ones on top. You worked hard on it."
Suraj rose on tiptoe, chest out, and beamed. Then he grabbed a handful of blocks from the box.
"Now I make it taller!"

qa.q: Which blocks did Suraj put at the bottom of the tower?
qa.a: He put the big blocks at the bottom.

qa.q: What is Suraj feeling when he shouts "look at me"?
qa.a: He feels tall, happy and proud, which shows in his tiptoes, out-pushed chest and beam. 🙂

qa.q: Why was Wasim's reply useful for Suraj?
qa.a: Wasim described what was there and named the hard work, so the pride felt real and Suraj wanted to try something bigger.

qa.q: How might Wasim see Suraj's tower?
qa.a: Wasim seems to see real effort and thinking in it, pointing out the big blocks below and small ones above.

grounding: A child builds a tower alone and shouts 'look at me', and the teacher describes what is there and names the hard work.

passage:
Tuesday: Ankita's block tower fell over at five blocks. She kicked it.
Thursday: She built it to eight blocks. It wobbled and fell. She built it again, slower this time, pressing each block down.
Saturday: Twelve blocks, straight and tall. "Look at me! Look at me!" she shouted, jumping. Her cousin Ishita came running. She didn't just say "good". She looked closely. "You made the bottom really wide, so it doesn't wobble. You worked hard on it." Ankita stood as tall as the tower. "Tomorrow I'll make fifteen!"

qa.q: How many blocks tall was Ankita's tower on Saturday?
qa.a: It was twelve blocks, straight and tall.

qa.q: How did Ankita feel when she shouted "Look at me!"?
qa.a: She felt proud and happy, as tall as her tower after trying all week.

qa.q: What did Ishita do that makes pride grow?
qa.a: She looked closely and described what Ankita did, the wide bottom and her hard work, instead of just saying "good".

qa.q: How might Ishita feel watching Ankita jump?
qa.a: She probably feels happy and excited for her cousin. 🎉

grounding: Over a week, a young girl finally builds a tall tower alone, feels proud, and her cousin describes the effort she sees.

passage: Madhav's room was tiny, and his baby sister kept crawling towards his blocks. He built fast, guarding the tower with one arm. Up, up, up. It reached the windowsill. "Mummy! Look at me! I did it ALL BY MYSELF!" Leela came in with a basket of washing and stopped. She put it down and knelt. "Wow. You kept it standing even with the baby crawling around. And you put the big blocks at the bottom. You worked hard on it." Madhav grinned so much his cheeks hurt. "Now I'm going to build a bridge too."

qa.q: How high did Madhav's tower reach?
How was Madhav feeling when he shouted for Mummy?
qa.a: He felt proud and happy, excited that he had done it all by himself.

qa.q: Why did Leela's words work better than a quick "good job"?
qa.a: She noticed the real details and his effort, which made his pride feel seen and made him want to try more.

qa.q: What is it like for Leela to stop her work and kneel?
qa.a: She likely feels glad and proud of Madhav, and wants him to know she noticed.

grounding: A young boy builds a tall tower despite his baby sister nearby, shouts for his mother, and she describes his effort.
